lens: Performance — latency, throughput, complexity, hot-path impact
answer: PR #12 is a pure path-rewrite + file-deletion + ADR addition. No algorithm, data structure, or hot-path logic was modified. Analysis of each F8 judge question: (1) expected_scalar_fields — not touched; validation complexity unchanged, O(n) over fixed schema set. (2) Repo cold-start / build cost — .audit/agent-read.jsonl (130 JSONL lines, ~52 KB) deleted and gitignored. Net effect: slightly faster cold clone and workspace restore; no build-script involvement. (3) Argo GitOps reconcile cost — path moved from deploy/gitops/oya-vcs-admission to infra/kyverno/oya-vcs-admission; one Argo Application object, reconcile cycle count unchanged; string constant rewrite in Rust is a compile-time literal, zero runtime delta. (4) New cargo deps or build-script triggers — none introduced; Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock untouched in this PR. Two crates (oya-foundry-vcs-provider-execution-gate-kernel, -gate-app) recompile due to source changes but the change is a single &str constant swap, incremental recompile is trivial. No performance regression identified at any layer.
key_claims: No change to expected_scalar_fields or any validation loop — hot-path complexity class O(n) unchanged.
.audit/ deletion removes ~52 KB from tracked tree — marginally improves clone and index performance.
ARGO_MANIFEST constant is a compile-time &str; path rewrite carries zero runtime cost.
Argo CD reconcile rate is determined by the Application object count and sync interval, both unchanged.
No new Cargo dependencies or build.rs scripts introduced; Cargo.lock unmodified.
uncertainty_areas: Cannot confirm Argo sync interval configuration from diff alone; assumed unchanged (no Application spec fields other than path were modified).
Downstream Argo watch-resource overhead for infra/kyverno/ vs deploy/gitops/ tree depth is negligible but not benchmarked.

findings.summary: Marginal clone/restore improvement from removing ~52 KB tracked JSONL artifact (.audit/agent-read.jsonl).
findings.recommended_action: No action required; improvement is inherent to the deletion.
